source: The only element bringing me peace is the knowledge that your father's soul has ascended to Heaven.
I now believe it is in our collective interest to ensure Hamlet can never harm another.
Rest assured-- he will be dealt with in swift time.
I have reason to believe Hamlet may act in violence against my father.
What? Where? And when?
In...in the Queen's chambers, my lord. I know not why.
Wah hah hah! I'd like to see him try. My nephew's a half-wit with any weapon in his hand.
And who could ever bear your father ill will, of all people?
Have you spoken to my wife of these fears?
She has far more patience and love for you than I.
We need to discuss something.
Hamlet killed my father in cold blood. And he's going to do it again.
I warned him to stay his hand, but he listened not.
Grow used to the sting of loss, Ophelia. You will see it yet many hundreds of times before you are free.
Bernardo. You're someone I know I can trust.
I believe Hamlet may act in violence against my father. Can you protect Father from harm?
I can't speak about this right now, my lady. Apologies for being evasive, but -- many things have taken place in the last few hours.
I'll find you again very soon.
You should no longer affix such honor to me, my lady.
I will spend every night the rest of my life wondering why I wasn't there to stop Hamlet in time.
I grieve for your father. And my deepest condolences go out to you and to Laertes.
For what it's worth, he was kind to me as a child in ways my own father never was.
I loved him too. I loved him dearly. And I will never forget the kindness he showed me.
Er... And where do you believe this violence may take place, precisely?
In the Queen's private chambers.
Hamlet has visited his mother's chambers a hundred times before without issue...
Why now? What could have changed? What was he thinking?
Why do you believe him to be a murderer now?
I can't explain it, Bernardo. But please—in all the years we've known each other, have you not learned to trust me?
...If it will put your mind at ease, I will ensure no one comes to harm in the Queen's chambers.
You have my word.
Thank you. Thank you eternally.
Laertes, what if I told you I knew Hamlet would kill Father?
Premonitions are useless to the both of us now.
Father is dead. Mother is dead.
I will bury him beside her.
And you and I, we live on. We must never lose sight of each other's back. Not now. Not ever.
I want Hamlet dead. The Queen merely wants him gone. We shall see which of us perserveres first.
You know Hamlet to be capable of intense anger—
And intense inaction. The man couldn't determine what to eat for supper, let alone plot to take down Father.
But what if he got angry? He's been unhinged as of late. What might he do then?
I don't know how to convince you, but I tell you the truth. Hamlet will take Father's life.
I do believe you in my heart, Ophelia. That's why I've decided to stay.
I will watch for the slightest sign of aggression in him. If I find him to threaten Father in any way, I'll not hesitate to act.
I promise you that.
Irma, we ought to talk about Hamlet.
You've heard the news by now, I'm sure.
Oh, Ophelia. Oh, my little bird. I felt your pain from far away the instant I found out.
My heart aches for you and your brother.
Had Hamlet been... properly disciplined before now-- had someone intervened-- your father might yet live.
I believe Hamlet may act violently against my father.
And I certainly believe it.
He is murderous, uncontrollable. Everyone in Elsinore is afraid.
Perhaps someone his elder can calm him. Speak to him of his rage.
He pushes away my lady and his uncle with all his might.
But... perhaps someone else could... intervene.
I have to stop Hamlet.
You truly are an amateur at this, aren't you?
And here I thought that the most basic of endeavours in this world!
Regardless, of course, the right performance could urge Hamlet to remain seated...
Such a quandary. Truly. If only there were some way it could be prevented!
Perhaps the right performance could urge the unruly boy to remain seated...
I sense that you may have some familiarity my work, already.
If you are interested in seeing me perform something special, perhaps based upon some juicy gossip, you might consider a collaboration!
I believe there's an assassin embedded into the members of the court, trying to have me killed.
Oho! What a fascinating topic for a performance. Lavish, dangerous, exquisite... a tale of daggers lodged in spines!
Unfortunately, you've missed your chance.
That window of opportunity has, shall we say, been shut. I hope you enjoyed the performance.
Hee hee. What great havoc shall we wreak with this juicy performance, dear?
I'll let you find out!
Oho! What a fascinating topic for our upcoming production. Let's put on something lavish, dangerous, exquisite... a tale of daggers lodged in spines!
Hamlet is acting unusually strangely.
Oho! What a fascinating topic for a production. Unfortunately, you've missed your chance.
Oh, indeed? I simply must work a brooding prince into my upcoming production. I have so, so many ideas...
I've heard that the Queen had an affair with King Claudius before her husband's death.
They say the best drama is born of scandal, my dear!—Or at least, I do. I say that. Perhaps I can use this information in our upcoming performance.
I'm certain that King Claudius murdered his own brother.
Hee hee. What great havoc shall we wreak with this juicy performance?
Hmm. What a fascinating proposal... perhaps I can use this in my upcoming performance. It is a classic murder story, after all, isn't it? Even perhaps, hmm, a bit overdone.
I believe I'm reliving the same days over and over again, as if time is repeating...
Hee hee. What great havoc shall we wreak this time, dear?
How peculiar and yet wonderful. But have you figured out the reason for the repetition yet?
Without a motive, you'll keep uncovering the same tortuous twists and turns, failing to save everyone...
Oh, I spoke out of turn! Terribly sorry.
I have a most fascinating performance to put on, inspired by you!
My father will die, and none of the royal family will mourn him—not even the King. If he knew that, maybe he wouldn't sacrifice himself for the Queen.
Ahh, a daughter's love. Such a tender little thing.
Yes, yes! Shall we see how this alters the course of history? I admit, I'm most curious!
I have a most fascinating performance to put on, inspired by you.
Your lady-in-waiting Brit is a spy for the Prince of Norway.
I know. I can hardly believe it.
You think you know someone, Ophelia, and then...
I knew she was unhappy. But to this extent-- to the point of treason? How can it be?
I think someone must have put her up to this.
She is too young to have chosen this for herself. I know it in my heart.
Damn that father of hers.
My little Brit? Ha!
I tell the truth, my lady. In fact, I think you'll find proof on her if you only look for it.
That's quite a grave accusation, Ophelia.
And rather a stretch of an accusation, truth be told.
She does act strangely sometimes, but I'm sure it's nothing that can't be easily cleared up.
Why don't you ask the good Guard Captain to speak with her, if you're so worried?
Brit, I know you've been leaking information to Fortinbras.
Really? Is it because I just told you that?
You're a special kind of something, 'Feely.
I want you to help me stop the Prince from invading. I won't tell anyone you helped me.
That contraption was set into motion long before I was involved, 'Feely. The Prince has been plotting with my father for months.
There's got to be a way, Brit. I'm not asking for you to betray your father. Only to help me save lives.
I'm begging you. Please.
...There might be a way. But you won't like it.
They meet late at night in the town square, long after all are asleep. They plan to meet next right before the seige begins on Sunday.
Understood. I won't expose you, Brit. I promise.
Does anyone else know?
I suppose it doesn't matter. I knew this would come eventually.
Let them hang me, then. Go on. Run and tell the King. Let him snap my neck himself.
The best part is, Claudius is too proud to see it. He thinks he's extending an olive branch. All he's doing is exposing his back.
Then how can he be convinced?
I don't know! I don't know. Why does everyone expect me to have the answers here? I'm just a pawn! What choice do I have?
I hate this place. And I hate you especially. I wish you'd all leave me alone.
(Perhaps that would have gone better if I'd found a way to earn her trust first.)
(It's odd to speak with Brit like this, knowing she'd kill me if she had to...)
(Maybe we don't have to be this way—she and I. Maybe there's another option.)
...There is a way. But you won't like it.
I don't want you to be executed, believe it or not.
Then why are you speaking to me about this? Why not just turn me into the King directly? Did you... learn something?
Your Majesty, I know that Lady Brit is a spy, leaking information to Prince Fortinbras.
I'm aware. Bernardo is dealing with her as we speak. And to think that we had such a rat in our own court!
I understand you were the one who brought this to our attention.
It appears you are as clever as your are beautiful. I was truly a fool to have underestimated you for so long.
Lady Birgitta? Are you certain?
Of course, my king.
If this was coming from any woman but you, Ophelia, I'd laugh off the notion. But...
I promise you, I will make sure this information reaches the Guard Captain.
However, I'm sure she must have been acting of her own accord.
We're in the middle of peace negotiations with the Prince. There's no reason for him to spy on my court.
It's good that we never offered peace to Fortinbras. It's clear he cannot be trusted.
That's ridiculous. We're in the middle of peace negotiations with the Prince. There's no reason for him to spy on my court.
And Brit? She's but a girl like yourself! What could she possibly have to do with grand political schemes?
